record.paper_title: Open Problems for Entire Functions of Bounded Index in Direction
record.context_brief: Logarithmic derivative and zero counting criterion
record.original_question: Let F be entire on C^n and L be in Q_b^n. For each b-line t -> F(z0+tb), let G_r^b(F) be the union of scaled r-neighborhoods, measured with L, around the zeros of these one-variable slices. Is F of bounded L-index in direction b if and only if there is a single r > 0 and constants P > 0 and n_tilde such that (1) outside G_r^b(F), the logarithmic directional derivative satisfies |D_b F(z)/F(z)| <= P L(z), and (2) on every nonzero slice t -> F(z0+tb), each scaled disc of radius r/(|b| L(z0+t0 b)) contains at most n_tilde zeros?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n\ge 2$ and let $\mathbf{b}\in\mathbb{C}^n\setminus\{0\}$. Let $Q_{\mathbf b}^n$ denote the class of positive continuous functions $L:\mathbb{C}^n\to(0,\infty)$ such that for every $R>0$ there is a constant $\lambda(R)\ge 1$ with
\[ \lambda(R)^{-1}\le \frac{L(z+t\mathbf b)}{L(z)}\le \lambda(R) \qquad \text{whenever } z\in\mathbb{C}^n,\ t\in\mathbb{C},\ |t|\le R/(|\mathbf b|\,L(z)). \]
For an entire function $F:\mathbb{C}^n\to\mathbb{C}$ and $L\in Q_{\mathbf b}^n$, define the directional derivatives
\[ D_{\mathbf b}^0 F(z)=F(z),\qquad D_{\mathbf b}^{k+1}F(z)=\sum_{j=1}^n b_j\,\partial_{z_j}(D_{\mathbf b}^k F)(z). \]
$F$ is said to be of bounded $L$-index in the direction $\mathbf b$ if there exists $N\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$ such that for every $z\in\mathbb{C}^n$ and every $k\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$,
\[ \frac{|D_{\mathbf b}^k F(z)|}{k!\,L(z)^k}\le \max_{0\le j\le N}\frac{|D_{\mathbf b}^j F(z)|}{j!\,L(z)^j}. \]
For $r>0$ and $z_0\in\mathbb{C}^n$, set
\[ G_r^{\mathbf b}(F)=\bigcup_{z_0\in\mathbb{C}^n}\bigcup_{t_0\in Z_{z_0}}\Bigl\{ z_0+t\mathbf b:\ |t-t_0|\le \tfrac{r}{|\mathbf b|\,L(z_0+t_0\mathbf b)}\Bigr\}, \]
where $Z_{z_0}=\{t\in\mathbb{C}: F(z_0+t\mathbf b)=0\}$ when $F(z_0+\cdot\,\mathbf b)\not\equiv 0$ (and is empty otherwise).

Question: Is it true that $F$ is of bounded $L$-index in the direction $\mathbf b$ if and only if there exist a single $r>0$, a constant $P>0$, and a nonnegative integer $\tilde n$ such that:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(1)] for every $z\in\mathbb{C}^n\setminus G_r^{\mathbf b}(F)$ with $F(z)\ne 0$,
\[ \Bigl|\frac{D_{\mathbf b}F(z)}{F(z)}\Bigr|\le P\,L(z); \]
\item[(2)] for every $z_0\in\mathbb{C}^n$ with $F(z_0+\cdot\,\mathbf b)\not\equiv 0$ and every $t_0\in\mathbb{C}$, the disc $\{t\in\mathbb{C}:|t-t_0|\le r/(|\mathbf b|\,L(z_0+t_0\mathbf b))\}$ contains at most $\tilde n$ zeros of $t\mapsto F(z_0+t\mathbf b)$ (counted with multiplicity)?
\end{enumerate}
artifact.status_search_result: Closely related logarithmic-derivative and zero-distribution criteria for entire functions of bounded L-index in a direction have been established by Bandura and Skaskiv (e.g., Ukrainian Math. J. 2017 and subsequent works), and analogous criteria have been proved for slice holomorphic functions and for functions in the unit ball. The exact equivalence as stated, using a single value of r, does not appear to be explicitly settled in the published literature found, so the precise formulation remains, at most, partially resolved.

status_evidence.title: Directional Logarithmic Derivative and the Distribution of Zeros of an Entire Function of Bounded L-Index Along the Direction
status_evidence.snippet: An analog of the logarithmic criterion was proved, describing estimates of the logarithmic derivative outside exceptional sets generated by unions of slice discs.
status_evidence.claim: Logarithmic-derivative and zero-distribution criteria for bounded L-index in a direction have been established, supporting partial resolution.

status_evidence.title: Some criteria of boundedness of the L-index in direction for slice holomorphic functions of several complex variables
status_evidence.snippet: Criteria describing local behavior of maximum and minimum moduli, estimates of logarithmic derivatives and zero distributions.
status_evidence.claim: Analogous criteria have been extended to slice holomorphic functions of several complex variables.
